Noncritical Belyi Maps
Shinichi Mochizuki
May 2004
/BT/CQ/D7/D8/D6/CP /CR/D8/BA In the present paper, we present a slightly strengthened version of a
well-known theorem of Belyi on the existence of “Belyi maps” . Roughly speaking,
this strengthened version asserts that there exist Belyi maps which are unramiﬁed
at [cf. Theorem 2.5] — or even near [cf. Corollary 3.2] — a prescribed ﬁnite set of
points.

Corollary 1.2. (Belyi Opens as a Zariski Base) If VX ⊆ X is any open
subscheme of X containing a closed point x ∈ X, then there exists a Belyi open
UX ⊆ VX ⊆ X such that x ∈ UX. In particular, the Belyi opens of X form a base
for the Zariski topology of X.
